operating_notes.text: Global advances crossed ₹7.71 lakh Cr, growing 15.82% YoY.
Global advances crossed ₹7.71 lakh Cr, growing 15.82% YoY in FY26.
Bank of India increased its equity stake in associate ASREC (India) Ltd from 26.02% to 27.30% via a ₹22.64 crore capital infusion.
Global business grew 14.57% YoY to ₹16.98 lakh crore in Mar'26.
RAM advances increased 19.11% YoY to ₹3.84 lakh crore, constituting 58.74% of total advances.
Corporate and international loan pipeline is about ₹70,000 Cr within a total pipeline of more than ₹1 lakh crore.
International business crossed ₹2.5 lakh crore for the first time, closing at about ₹2.56 lakh crore, of which around 32% is low-margin trade finance being replaced.
ECLGS sanctions of about ₹6,000 Cr with ₹4,600 Cr disbursed; management expects about ₹8,000 Cr of sanctions by scheme end.
Global business crossed ₹18.92 lakh crore as of September 30, 2026.

watchlist.text: Shareholder approval for dividend at AGM

watchlist.response: Said majority of the $200 million raised so far is core FCNR with little leverage, but declined to quantify the leverage spread, calling it a moving target.
watchlist.text: Sushil Choksey asked what portion of the $1.2 billion FCNR target would be leveraged versus direct deposits, and what spread the leverage carries.

watchlist.response: Said PSL income opportunity exists in Q2 and Q3 but gave no number; said there are no plans for an AS15 reversal.
watchlist.text: Lavish (Morgan Stanley) asked how PSL income would trend after ₹277 Cr in Q1 and whether an AS15 provision reversal was planned.

watchlist.response: Gave ROA 1%+, NIM 2.55–2.60% and CIR 48–49% for FY27, implying the Q1 cost ratio is not expected to repeat.
watchlist.text: Nitin (Aurum Capital) asked for FY27 guidance on ROA, NIM and cost to income and whether 2.52% NIM and 46.3% CIR can be held in Q2.

watchlist.response: Attributed it to a structural shift in savings into equities and mutual funds, plus bulk deposits taken to fund credit growth, offset by cheaper 3–25 Cr fixed deposits.
watchlist.text: Sharad Chandra asked why CASA and retail term deposit shares each fell about 3% while cost of deposits still fell 15 bps.
